2: name: ui-plugin-development
3: description: Inspect or customize UI Plugins; propose missing project capabilities through a bounded user-confirmed development plan, reusing existing approved scopes.

6: ---
7: 
8: # UI Plugin development
9: 
10: This Skill applies to frontend Plugin source/application authoring. The system
11: prompt owns general evidence, authorization and completion rules; this Skill
12: adds Plugin-specific contracts, not an additional investigation checklist.
13: Use the smallest relevant section/reference. A resolved existing target does not
14: require a full capability inventory, a new UI-system decision or a nearest
15: consumer example before it can be modified.
16: 
17: ## Ownership and admission
18: 
19: Project-owned application props, children, renderers and scoped styles are ordinary
20: editable code. Inspect the exact target and any concrete unknown contract; edit
21: within the user's request. Public npm component use does not require implementation
22: source, extraction or takeover. Existing source-owned Plugin edits keep the current
23: ownership, upstream provenance and BASE; do not repeat successful takeover consent.
24: Only actual npm implementation edits require `takeover_plugin_source` and its
25: explicit user agreement. Canonical Runtime/Context, vendor and generated registries
26: remain protected. A thin wrapper's omitted public seam is not justification for
27: requiring takeover.
28: 
29: Before first new Plugin source or new business behavior, the Host must authorize
30: the bounded `prepare_ui_plugin_development` plan through its actual start/adjust/defer
31: question. The current request identifies the desired work, not approval of an
32: unseen implementation plan; a matching approved plan is reused without asking again. A normal existing
33: Plugin customization does not need a new development approval. Once the relevant API/source lacks the behavior, propose a bounded implementation;
34: do not search for the same missing operation in unrelated components. Required Service
35: contracts may be included as relatedServices in that one decision. For a genuinely new
36: Plugin, consult [authoring contracts](references/authoring-contracts.md) for admission,
37: manifest/placement, Service/data and delivery obligations. For a new visual Plugin
38: or actual UI-system choice also consult [UI selection](references/default-ui-composition.md).
39: Do not load new-Plugin investigation requirements for a local presentation repair.
40: 
41: ## Local change evidence
42: 
43: Read the existing files that will change, using the actual supplied sourceRoot and
44: owner paths. `manifest.json` declares identity/data/capabilities; `definition.ts`
45: joins manifest and component; `index.tsx` owns composition/behavior; imported
46: stylesheets own presentation. Read a neighboring consumer only for wiring that
47: is actually unknown. An npm implementation need not appear in local search.
48: 
49: `inspect_ui_plugin` returns application ownership, public APIs and parent semantic
50: composition where declared. sharedModule selects the installed public module;
51: use the root module for presentation controls and /contracts for Plugin types.
52: Use returned parameterContracts; follow exact parameterQueries only when a required
53: signature is missing. `$element` accesses an array/index element, not React props.
54: An unavailable guessed symbol is not a missing capability. Preserve declared
55: composition slots when appending controls; replacement props can replace them.
56: 
57: Public types establish invocation shape, not rendered styling. Package-owned
58: presentationContract describes raw versus styled components, asset requirements
59: and Portal ownership. For a visual defect follow the current owned entry's CSS
60: imports and inspect the relevant cascade. Re-querying types cannot establish
61: centering. Public overlay composites may own their own Portal and Backdrop;
62: respect that composition and retain the existing AgentUIRoot theme container.
63: Use the public Trigger/Close/focus APIs. Local dialog state or scoped popup
64: positioning does not introduce a Service, Agent action, Runtime replacement or
65: source takeover. Verify requested placement, closing and focus in the actual Host.
66: 
67: ## Editing constraints
68: 
69: Freshly read existing edit targets in the current run; old messages/handoff are
70: navigation, not current read evidence. `edit_file_from_read` edits a stable range;
71: `edit_file` handles small local changes; `mutate_ui_plugin_source` makes one atomic
72: Plugin-local transaction with edit/create entries. Re-read and reconcile affected
73: files after stale-content errors. Do not hand-edit `registry.generated.ts`, the
74: AppUIModel JSON or composition-revision metadata; use their Host tools.
75: 
76: Preserve the target's UI library, enabled capabilities, scope bridge, semantic
77: slots and original approval/interrupt/error renderers. New user/screen-reader copy
78: uses the unified domain locale namespace with en-US/zh-CN parity; never patch
79: vendor for localization. Read locale targets when changing them, not for every
80: style edit. Do not invent new per-Plugin i18n or Service abstractions.
81: 
82: Styles must be imported and scoped to owned classes/data attributes; no global
83: resets, Host ancestor selectors, Runtime/Portal changes or vendor overrides.
84: Own box-sizing, min-width and responsive maximum size. Flex/grid children must
85: shrink and long text wrap; overlays need bounded dimensions appropriate to the
86: actual container. Static heuristics are not visual acceptance. The specialized
87: responsive-repair proposal tool is not currently exposed by any Creator tool
88: group. For ordinary authorized responsive CSS changes, freshly read the owned
89: stylesheet, use the available file-edit tools and validate the current revision.
90: If the user explicitly requests the unavailable specialized proposal tool,
91: explain that limitation; do not claim to have invoked it.
92: 
93: ## Validation and outcome
94: 
95: Validate source changes at the current revision; include the build for new visual
96: Plugins or dependency/style integration as required. Composition changes use fresh
97: AppUIModel evidence and normal Host mutation/verification tools. Creation/catalog
98: synchronization is not mounting: newly created capabilities must be composed when
99: requested, and the final revision validated. Consume checks already performed by
100: the Host rather than duplicating them. Respect returned repair limits.
101: 
102: Keep static, Runtime and browser evidence distinct. Current tests/types or empty
103: Runtime errors do not prove popup geometry, keyboard behavior or focus. Validate
104: the requested interactions using available authorized browser/test evidence; report
105: missing infrastructure or stale evidence precisely. Do not label incomplete work
106: as already satisfied or reopen unrelated discovery when verification is unavailable.

6: 
7: ## Creator Authoring Contract
8: 
9: Runtime-compatible, Composition-compatible, and Creator-operable are separate
10: decisions:
11: 
12: - Runtime-compatible means the Plugin can be activated by the UI Runtime.
13: - Composition-compatible means its Layout or child Slot contract is valid.
14: - Creator-operable means the Host can discover, add, and restore it
15:   deterministically.
16: 
17: The existing `manifest.authoring` fields are the Creator Authoring Contract.
18: Do not add `creatorReady`, a readiness score, or Plugin-specific Creator logic.
19: The Host derives readiness from the manifest, capabilities, and child Slot
20: contracts; it does not inspect React source to guess placement.
21: 
22: Before writing source, classify the Plugin and decide whether users should be
23: able to ask Creator to add or restore it:
24: 
25: - A visual Plugin intended for natural-language Add/Restore declares semantic
26:   `authoring.intents` and a deterministic `defaultPlacement`.
27: - A relative `before`/`after` `defaultPlacement` requires
28:   `recommendedSize.width`.
29: - A relative `above`/`below` `defaultPlacement` requires
30:   `recommendedSize.height`.
31: - Before choosing a relative placement, inspect the anchor's current Layout
32:   parent. `before`/`after` require an existing Row or root anchor;
33:   `above`/`below` require an existing Column or root anchor. An anchor inside
34:   a root Row cannot use `below` through `insert_plugin_default`. If no
35:   supported default fits the requested UI, use the low-level AppUIModel path
36:   after reading its Skill instead of declaring an unusable default.
37: - A `plugin_slot` placement points at an existing parent child Slot, matches
38:   one of that Slot's accepted capabilities, and matches renderer mode.
39: - A Plugin with `requiresRenderScope: true` uses a renderer child Slot; a
40:   non-renderer Plugin must not target one.
41: - A visual Plugin without `authoring` is intentionally `manual-only` and is
42:   valid. `authoring` without `defaultPlacement` is discoverable but
43:   `limited`, with Add/Restore unavailable.
44: - A Plugin with `capabilities: ["headless"]` or `manifest.application.gate` is
45:   not a visual placement target and does not need authoring metadata.

47: Read the readiness diagnostics returned by `validate_creator_changes` through
48: the existing `verify:ui` result. A limited warning is not automatically a
49: failure: if the Plugin should be Creator-operable, repair its authoring
50: contract; if it is intentionally manual-only, do not invent a placement.

53: ## Service dependency and ownership decision
54: 
55: When a Plugin needs another capability, call `inspect_ui_services` instead of
56: guessing a Provider from Plugin names or source proximity.
57: 
58: ```text
59: Plugin needs capability X
60: -> inspect_ui_services
61: -> existing Service?
62:    -> yes: classify core requirement as inject, enhancement as optionalInject
63:    -> no: is a cross-boundary shared Service actually necessary?
64:       -> no: keep the behavior private to the Plugin
65:       -> yes: resolve the natural Owner, exact Consumers and dependency modes
66:               -> prepare_ui_service_contract_change
67:               -> confirmation-required: ask the User and stop project writes
68:               -> authorized: create_ui_service_contract
69:                  -> wire Provider and Consumers
70:                  -> validate, then Runtime verify only in static_and_runtime mode
71: ```
72: 
73: - `inject` is only for a capability without which the Plugin's core behavior cannot work.
74: - `optionalInject` is for an enhancement with a complete fallback when the Service is unavailable.
75: - A missing optional Service is not permission to create it. Omit the dependency unless the user explicitly authorizes a new shared capability.
76: - A new Plugin does not declare `provides` merely because another Plugin might use its behavior later.
77: - Required Service contracts may be included in `relatedServices` of the Plugin
78:   development proposal. The Host checks owner/consumer topology and contract paths,
79:   shows them in the same user decision and returns scoped Service authorization IDs.
80:   Use those IDs with the existing create/mutate Service tools; do not ask again for
81:   that same scope. Other Services remain unauthorized.
82: - Standalone Service proposals still require a real Host question. Model text or
83:   a service name in the user request does not approve an unseen concrete plan.
84: - To change an existing Service Contract, inspect all `contractPaths`, Providers and Consumers, require one canonical path, read that file, authorize the exact impact, then use `mutate_ui_service_contract` exact edits and update affected Plugins.
85: - Generic `edit_file` and Plugin tools never write `/services/**`; only authorized Service Contract tools may do so.
86: - A public Service is justified only across a real boundary: multiple Plugins, another Plugin caller, Application Shell, or a Frontend Tool/Agent adapter. Private state and helpers stay inside the Plugin.

89: ## Creating a Plugin
90: 
91: 1. Classify the Plugin, decide whether it should be Creator-operable, and define its Runtime, Composition, and optional Creator Authoring contracts.
92: 2. Use the installed public `UIPluginDefinition`, `UIPluginManifest` and
93:    `UIPluginComponentProps` contracts from `@za38.03/agent-ui-plugins/contracts`.
94:    For unresolved fields, query those symbols through `inspect_ui_plugin` with
95:    that `sharedModule`. Current Bootstrap projects do not contain
96:    `/framework/contracts/ui-plugin.ts`. A nearby thin application is sufficient
97:    evidence for registration and locale conventions; do not search for a fully
98:    copied official implementation. A self-contained local-state Plugin needs
99:    only the relevant component, manifest and optional child-Slot contracts.

For a new visible Plugin, draft its manifest and call `preflight_ui_plugin_placement` with the current AppUIModel hash, capability catalog revision, and intended instance id before writing source. Use its canonical `defaultPlacement` only if it matches the user's location and lifecycle. A rejection requires a same-semantics repair or a user decision; do not switch to application scope, another side, or a conditional Slot as fallback. Preflight does not verify source, Services, or narrow Runtime geometry, and the final mutation checks again. Once eligible, proceed to locale edits and the atomic `create_ui_plugin` call; further source searches need a specific unresolved API.

102:    `data.messages`, `data.state`, and `data.messageUI` are booleans for AG-UI subscriptions; `data.events` is an array of event names. Local React `useState` is private Plugin state and does not belong in `manifest.data`.

When an existing project component implements the requested UI, this may be a thin adapter importing it; do not recreate that UI for Plugin self-containment. Accept `UIPluginComponentProps` only when it needs `renderSlot`; read Agent and instance data through Runtime Context hooks in the adapter and narrow unknown state safely.

105:    Import the component with `from "./index"` when it lives in the required `index.tsx`. Do not also create `index.ts` as a barrel: TypeScript resolves `./index` to that file first and can make the component import circular. 114:     eligible relative `defaultPlacement` declares the intended side panel,

117:     the conversation's existing Slot or nest a Row inside its Panel. Use a
118:     low-level Layout operation only for a different authorized location after
119:     checking its root track and responsive contract. An Application Gate goes
120:     at application scope. The transaction updates the generated Registry.

125: ## Contract boundaries
126: 
127: ### Application Gate contract
128: 
129: Use `manifest.application.gate` when entry to the Workspace must be denied until a condition is ready. Do not model this requirement as a modal, overlay, root/main Slot contribution, dedicated Login Slot, or high-z-index element, and do not change the Layout Tree merely to host it.
130: 
131: - The Gate manifest names one observable Service and may assign a numeric priority. Do not also add an `app-gate` capability; `application.gate` is the single source of truth and is distinct from `headless`.
132: - The definition declares the Gate Service in `provides`, and `setup()` synchronously provides it with an initial `checking`, `blocked`, `ready`, or `error` snapshot. Async session recovery begins only after the observable Service is available.
133: - A Gate plugin node is `enabled: true` in `applicationPlugins`. A Gate manifest must not declare child Slots.
134: - Gate hard dependencies use `inject`. Every Provider in that dependency closure must be an application-scoped `headless` Plugin or another Application Gate. `optionalInject` never expands the startup dependency closure.
135: - The Gate component may read its own provided Gate Service with `usePluginService()`. This self-read permission applies to Components only; `setup({ services }).get()` still reads only `inject` and `optionalInject` dependencies.
136: - Multiple Gates all must become `ready`. Priority selects which non-ready Gate surface is currently displayed; it does not weaken the all-ready rule.
137: - Gate state is frontend Application lifecycle state. Never add AG-UI custom events or modify Agent protocol semantics to control it.
138: 
139: For requests such as “不登录不能进入应用”, “打开应用必须先登录”, “没有 License 不能使用”, “必须先选择组织”, or “初始化完成前不能进入工作台”, inspect existing Gate/Auth assets and Services first, then create or reuse an Application Gate without introducing a Login Slot or Layout overlay.
140: 
141: ### Child Slot contract
142: 
143: When adding, removing, or renaming a child `renderSlot(...)` outlet in a container Plugin, update `manifest.json` `slots.children` in the same task. Each local Slot name maps to a required `description`, `cardinality: "one" | "many"`, and optional `optional` flag. Names must be static string literals; do not create dynamic `renderSlot(slot)` outlets or global Runtime slot ids. Host verification treats the Plugin source and manifest child Slot sets as an exact contract.
144: 
145: For an npm-backed Plugin, the project application may add a new semantic outlet
146: without source takeover. Preserve every installed canonical child Slot unchanged,
147: declare the additional Slot in the local manifest, expose that combined manifest
148: from the local definition, and render the new outlet explicitly in the application.
149: Keep forwarding the original props and Slots into the npm component. The Host
150: combines only the additional local Slots with the installed canonical contract;
151: the npm component does not implicitly render project-added outlets.
152: 
153: For a runtime entity renderer, declare `mode: "renderer"`, `cardinality: "one"`, and `accepts.anyOfCapabilities`, then call `renderScopedSlot("localName", scope)`. Renderer Slots have no implicit presentation fallback. A fallback must be explicitly supplied by the owning parent; otherwise an empty, disabled, unavailable, inactive, or capability-mismatched occupant renders nothing. Omitted `mode` means ordinary content. The renderer Plugin reads `usePluginRenderScope()` and checks its `kind`; a Plugin that requires scope declares `requiresRenderScope: true` and returns `null` without the expected scope. Prefer changing the renderer Plugin instance in AppUIModel when changing Reasoning, Tool Group, or Tool Fallback presentation. Keep Agent UI grouping, part order, named Tool UI selection, and message lifecycle in the canonical Thread.
154: 
155: - Read Agent data through the installed Runtime public APIs and the project's existing domain/Service Hooks. Inspect their actual exports and signatures; initialized projects do not contain a local `/runtime/context` module. Keep the existing Provider and canonical Conversation Runtime.
156: - Read the current instance scope through `usePluginInstance`, `usePluginActions`, and `usePluginEvents`. Never recreate a combined context prop or pass Runtime snapshot fields through component props.
157: - Before a Plugin consumes a backend Application Event, inspect the existing `Agent.appEventSchemas` binding and `/agent-contract/agent-events.ts` when present, reuse or add the application-owned payload schema, then declare the same exact name in `manifest.data.events`. Preserve an explicitly supplied Custom Event name exactly; lowercase dot-separated naming is recommended only when the application has not already chosen a name. A manifest declaration consumes an application-owned contract; it does not register one.
158: - Prefer the project-local `subscribeAppEvent` helper so the registered payload type is inferred; `usePluginEvents().subscribe` and `setup({ events })` remain the underlying scoped APIs. Never import AG-UI protocol event types into Plugin code, invent a schema inside a Plugin, emit an Application Event from the frontend, or use this channel for persistent state, standard lifecycle, Activity, interrupts, Frontend Tools, or local Plugin communication. If the backend payload contract is unknown, ask for it instead of inventing fields.
159: - Use `usePluginActions()` for instance-scoped Agent commands and the installed Runtime's public Host API for application-owned commands. Keep transient UI state out of AppUIModel; use private component state within one Plugin and Services across Plugins. Never create a separate Agent Runtime inside a Plugin.
160: - Keep Plugin dependencies in the generated project and follow its current UI stack and versions.
161: - Service contracts are stable project-owned capability seams, not concrete
162:   Provider Plugins or Runtime Core actions:
163:   - `provides` means this Plugin owns and declares one or more capabilities for the current activation lifecycle.
164:   - `inject` means this Plugin requires a hard capability dependency before activation.
165:   - `optionalInject` means this Plugin can use an enhancement but remains complete and active without it.
166:   - `usePluginService()` is runtime capability lookup for component access; `setup({ services })` remains the non-React activation API.
167: - Provider rules are strict: if `setup` calls `services.provide`, the Plugin **must** declare the same Service Name in `UIPluginDefinition.provides`.
168: - For a hard capability dependency, import its stable Service seam from `/services/*` and declare `inject` on `UIPluginDefinition`; do not import concrete Provider Plugin source.
169: - Provider implementations must be exposed only through `setup({ services })` + `services.provide(...)`, and the same Service Name must be declared in `provides`.
170: - Optional dependency behavior must declare `optionalInject`, call `usePluginService(...)`, and tolerate `undefined` with a complete fallback.
171: - `setup({ services }).get(X)` requires X to appear in `inject` or `optionalInject`. A component `usePluginService(X)` may also read a Service declared by its own definition in `provides`; Application-owned lookup remains unrestricted.
172: - `provides`, `inject`, and `optionalInject` are pairwise disjoint.
173: - When multiple Plugins share a capability, reuse an existing seam name/type from `/services/*` and never invent a synonym service contract.
174: - Prefer `UIPluginObservableService` only when other Plugins need sustained observation of service-owned state.
175: - `UIPluginObservableService` requires `getSnapshot()` + `subscribe()`; otherwise prefer a structural interface with explicit methods.
176: - Structural interface service examples are acceptable, and `EventEmitter`-style ad-hoc emitters should remain project-local, not runtime API additions.
177: - Do not place capability implementations into Plugin actions or Agent Runtime actions.
178: - A Frontend Tool is an Agent-facing adapter for a selected capability operation; it is not a Plugin capability and is not registered by a Plugin.
179: - When the product explicitly asks the Agent to invoke frontend behavior, first reuse an existing stable Service seam, have the Provider Plugin declare `provides`, and expose the selected operation from `/agent-contract/agent-tools.ts`. If no suitable seam exists, use the authorized Service ownership flow; never use `create_ui_plugin` or generic writes for `/services`.
180: - Frontend Tool names use `lower_snake_case`, inputs use `z.strictObject(...)`, descriptions explain when to call the Tool plus what it does and does not do, and results stay short, structured, and serializable.
181: - Frontend Tool handlers call `services.get(...)` and must tolerate a capability disappearing before execution. Never bind a Tool to a React component, ref, DOM query, Plugin instance, or concrete Provider implementation.
182: - Do not automatically expose every Service method. A Service may have zero, one, or many explicitly authorized Frontend Tools.
183: - Never generate `context.tools.register(...)`, `services.registerTool(...)`, `plugin.registerTool(...)`, or another Plugin self-registration API. Frontend Tool exposure is an Application permission boundary.
184: - Provider implementation lifetime is the Plugin activation lifetime; consumers should always read through runtime services instead of direct imports.
185: - Do not couple a generated Plugin to Creator packages or Creator UI dependencies.
186: - Do not modify `/runtime` or `/framework` for Plugin-specific behavior.
187: - Do not rewrite unrelated registration entries.
188: - Hiding, removing an instance, and replacing a feature all preserve Plugin source. Do not delete a Plugin directory with generic file tools. Permanent source deletion may only use the dedicated gated domain tool after exact authorization and reference checks; if that tool is unavailable, report the gate instead of approximating it.

192:

194: cross-boundary reason for a public Service seam: Plugin provides Service,

196: rules; Service existence does not grant Agent exposure permission.

206: ## Delivery obligations
207: 
208: For new-Plugin gap discovery, `inspect_ui_capabilities({})` returns two current
209: Operator results: plugins from list_ui_plugins and services from inspect_ui_services.
210: It has no detail or cursor parameters and does not include formal Source Items
211: or a project component index. Use inspect_agent_ui_sources separately for formal
212: resources and targeted file tools for project components. Do not infer absence
213: from this combined Plugin/Service result alone. Filenames never prove component
214: behavior. Inspect the selected implementation and reuse it whenever it fits.
215: 
216: A requested behavior absent from inspected public APIs/owned source is a design
217: and implementation gap, not a reason to find an identical existing example. Submit
218: `prepare_ui_plugin_development` for the user decision before writing. The Host
219: checks current Plugin identities and reuses current owner source evidence; formal
220: Source Item lookup is needed only for a relevant unknown resource.
221: 
222: For first new-Plugin implementation, provide `deliveryContract` to
223: `prepare_ui_plugin_development`: `capability`, `renderingCategory`, `placement`,
224: `lifecycle`, `dependencies`, `reusedComponents`, `verificationMethod`, and
225: `interactions`. `renderingCategory` is `panel`, `semantic-slot`, or `application`.
226: `verificationMethod` is `runtime` or `browser-test`. Bind placement to actual
227: current authoring choices. For requested dimensions/positions, include `geometry`
228: entries with `instanceId`, `property` (`x`, `y`, `width`, `height`), `expected`, and
229: `tolerance` in pixels. Do not change the Runtime manifest schema for this plan.

231: Creation, registration, enabled composition, static validation, Runtime observation,
232: and behavioral validation are separate facts. The Host completion gate derives
233: delivery from those facts at the current revision. `static_only` cannot establish
234: Runtime or interaction success. Missing placement or verification leaves a blocked
235: receipt naming saved changes and the last successful stage.

237: For declared interactions, the Host tool `verify_ui_plugin_behavior` runs the
238: project's installed Playwright configuration. Test titles must exactly match
239: `[delivery:<pluginId>] <interaction>`; use `runtime` when the browser-test method has
240: no interaction list. Every required test must pass without skips or flaky retries.
241: Reuse existing test infrastructure and respect the writable project boundary;
242: if tests/configuration cannot be supplied within that boundary, report the blocker.
243: Do not replace an absent browser test with a model-written PASS claim. Composer
244: adapters require send, stop, attachment add/remove/attachment-only send, and draft
245: parity for the capabilities already enabled in the target project.

248: ## Localization ownership
249: 
250: Vendor-owned code must remain locale-agnostic and unmodified; all product
251: localization is owned by AgentUICreator composition, adapters, plugins, and Host
252: UI. New user-visible copy must use the existing `useAgentUILocale` namespace and
253: complete `en-US` / `zh-CN` dictionaries. Do not create per-Plugin i18n hooks or
254: language conditionals. Preserve protocol IDs, enums, schema and persisted fields;
255: locale is a view concern. Prefer public props/composition, then owned adapters.
256: If upstream lacks a seam, record a localization gap instead of modifying vendor.

261: 
262: For Vue, HTML and legacy Hosts, discover/install the `web-component-bridge` compatibility resource through the existing resource protocol. React remains the canonical Plugin implementation.
